conversation.text: Owen, I can explain it all to you. You know how much I resent the way the old grudge got exposed after the red umbrella incident.

conversation.speaker: owen
conversation.text: Jules, Owen, can you prove the church bell didn't steal from the motel, you do your best to hide things when they happen.

conversation.speaker: jules
conversation.text: your idea that the church bell wasn't involved in the motel's fire is ridiculous and not based on anything at all.

conversation.speaker: mara
conversation.text: Fine, Jules, I wanted to win your attention during the old grudge over a red umbrella, and I resented everyone who got it first.

conversation.speaker: owen
conversation.text: Oh, yeah, and that night, some other idiot stole my brother's guitar, and we still argue over who broke the last one... over. Anyway, Jules, what made you feel I wanted to win your attention, exactly?

conversation.speaker: jules
conversation.text: Sarah, that's boring bullshit. If you want me to believe you, explain the night someone stole the church bell without hiding behind that polite little act.

conversation.speaker: sarah
conversation.text: I hate admitting this, Jules, but I'm scared you'll pick everyone else over me, and Herman's locked suitcase made it worse.

conversation.speaker: owen
conversation.text: Oh. Jules, I think you're forgetting something. When you want people to share and explore how our past shapes our future and we really need them to remember.

conversation.speaker: jules
conversation.text: The truth? I can think of an event that aligns perfectly with our memories of 'when things didn't go as planned' - 'Herman and Sarah went out into the snow that early...'

conversation.speaker: sarah
conversation.text: I wasn't talking about making someone get down to their birthday outfit or doing some crazy stunt in a blizzard, or pulling pranks, especially not this week... you were worried sick about her party going down last night.

conversation.speaker: mara
conversation.text: Oh, that ridiculous notion you two had about us!

conversation.speaker: jules
conversation.text: Nope, Sarah. You're being painfully safe. Tell me why the disputed tattoo pact happened or at least invent a better lie.

conversation.speaker: sarah
conversation.text: Oh girl, a laundromat is a terrible concept to tie to a disputed tattoo pact? Have a peek inside you. Here I see 'wallowing' a ridiculous incident or having one yourself at all?

conversation.speaker: mara
conversation.text: That's because it looks like a weak attempt to hide something you can't be seen by, a pathetic attempt at power.

conversation.speaker: owen
conversation.text: Enough, Mara. I'm not following you down another bullshit detour. Explain the fake engagement rumor or drop it.

conversation.speaker: sarah
conversation.text: Owen, don't give me that shit. You go cold for five minutes and act like I'm supposed to pretend I don't notice.

conversation.speaker: mara
conversation.text: Owen, don't let me catch your momentary lapse and act like I didn't notice, let's compare who is here for me, for my values, and my needs. I don't care if I'm not there; that's what makes me stronger.

conversation.speaker: owen
conversation.text: I'm done with this, Mara. I don't trust where you're taking it. Tell me what really happened with the restaurant they swear they were banned from.

conversation.speaker: jules
conversation.text: Here's the ugly truth, Owen: I liked the chaos around the vanished garden statue because everyone finally stopped being boring.

conversation.speaker: mara
conversation.text: It sounds like you think everyone needed something when Owen. Some people do make us wait to learn more when they think everyone finally stops being boring.

conversation.speaker: owen
conversation.text: That's rich coming out of you with the old grudge over the red umbrella.

conversation.speaker: jules
conversation.text: Here's the ugly truth, Mara: I liked the chaos around the birthday-cake sabotage because everyone finally stopped being boring.

conversation.speaker: sarah
conversation.text: That's what I thought you said when the garden statue fell into the lake.

conversation.speaker: owen
conversation.text: Sarah, this is exactly like the stolen brass flamingo: you act confused when it's convenient and expect everyone else to swallow it.

conversation.speaker: jules
conversation.text: I want you to leave my house, I need some air in here. But I don't just want to leave, I want you to take away something even bigger than that.

conversation.speaker: sarah
conversation.text: That's the whole point of our house, you're too much and that red umbrella is all that remains of that first fight. Your precious red umbrella, why are you making such a big deal out of it, it's nothing but a relic from the past.

conversation.speaker: mara
conversation.text: I have a secret too... about a weird incident when that little angel was younger... I tried to take it home too.
